name: Padanian nationalism
summary: Padanian nationalism claims that northern Italy forms a natural nation, Padania, exploited by a centralist, clientelist Roman state and its southern dependents. It demands fiscal federalism and self-rule, with independence as a final goal that was proclaimed in 1996. It combines regional libertarian and small-business politics with a defence of northern identity and hostility to illegal immigration and Islam.
scope: The Lega Nord-led Padanist movement from 1990s to roughly 2013, based on Bossi's 1996 declaration, Gianfranco Miglio's federalist writing as described in sources, and the party's programme. Excludes Salvini's national Lega and the Italian-nationalist turn after 2013, and the Veneto and Lombard autonomy movements as separate strands.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Lega Nord defended workers' pensions and public services for northerners, and regional healthcare is a standard autonomist competence, so mild support is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The party has no documented minimum-wage line; its small-business base and its labor-defending rhetoric pull in opposite directions.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The original programme called the ideology federalist libertarianism and the party backed deregulation and small business, though Bossi also called it partly socialist.

public-ownership.rationale: Deregulation and anti-statist rhetoric make nationalization unlikely, though no direct stance on utilities is documented.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The party adopted a flat tax at its 2014 congress and its grievance is northern taxation generally, so higher rates on the wealthy are unlikely.

unions-good.rationale: The party courted northern workers and defended wages but is rooted in employers and artisans, so adherents are split on unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Northern small-business and artisan constituencies make property protection a natural value, though it is inferred rather than stated.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-bureaucracy deregulation is a theme, though it is also described as anti-monopolist and anti-globalist, so the lean is only slight.

cut-welfare.rationale: The party attacks southern clientelist welfare spending yet defended pensions and workers, so cutting welfare as such is contested.

worker-ownership.rationale: No documented support for worker ownership; the movement is built on small proprietors and fiscal grievance rather than collectivism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: No documented position; its tough stance on migration and terrorism suggests security sympathy but libertarian rhetoric cuts against it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The party has been socially conservative and law-and-order oriented, so drug legalization is unlikely to be endorsed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The party's rhetoric about Islam and southerners has drawn complaints, and it presents itself as defying politically correct limits on speech.

strong-leader.rationale: Bossi's personal charismatic leadership was central, but the movement frames itself as a popular revolt, not as a call for bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: It attacks the Roman centralist state but wants to build a federal Padanian state with full state powers, so it rejects statelessness.

limit-guns.rationale: The party has been associated with a right-wing, law-and-order stance and pushed to ease self-defence law; strict gun limits are unlikely.

empower-police-military.rationale: The party pursued tough enforcement on migration under Interior Minister Maroni and a law-and-order line.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The party's socially conservative drift makes legalization unlikely, though no direct stance is documented.

decide-locally.rationale: The declaration accuses Rome of eroding the autonomy of municipalities, provinces and regions and demands that Padania hold all state powers.

rehabilitation.rationale: A law-and-order outlook favors punishment; inferred from its tough-on-crime stance.

traditional-family.rationale: The party moved toward a socially conservative approach after its early years.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The party's socially conservative turn suggests opposition, though position is inferred and early libertarian voices differed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the party's socially conservative and Catholic-leaning turn; no direct stance documented.

more-religion-public.rationale: The party swung between Celtic neo-paganism, anti-clericalism and pro-Church positions, so adherents are split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement's identity politics center on defending a native Padanian people against immigrants, not on remedying racial injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: A socially conservative approach implies rejecting this view; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The party shapes the identity of the Popolo Padano and presents Islam as a threat to Italian and Padanian identity and tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: The movement defined itself against the established party system in Rome and staged a unilateral independence declaration, though it later accepted reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anti-immigrant messaging drove the League's 2008 success and the party has always opposed illegal immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The party has been Eurosceptic and anti-globalist, though its declaration praised a Europe of the Regions.

free-trade.rationale: Anti-globalist rhetoric and small-business protectionist sympathies conflict with a libertarian programme.

nation-first.rationale: The party's slogans put northern interest first and it was anti-globalist and Eurosceptic.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: No documented stance; anti-immigrant and Eurosceptic outlook suggests reluctance to foreign interventions.

open-borders.rationale: Anti-immigrant messaging is central to the League's appeal.

limit-growth.rationale: The movement champions northern productive industry and small enterprise, which cuts against degrowth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Productive-north and anti-regulation outlook make drastic state climate action unlikely; no direct stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented view; the topic is outside the movement's concerns.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Italy rejected nuclear power by referendum and the party has no settled core position.

revolution-justified.rationale: The declaration was a symbolic secession invoking self-determination, though the party works through elections.

experts-over-public.rationale: The movement is populist and anti-elite, framing itself against the Roman political class.

central-planning.rationale: The party stresses small business, deregulation and flat tax and attacks Roman statism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not documented; its libertarian-leaning economic programme does not favor public or worker ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: It favors flat tax and cutting tax burdens, not a single land tax; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Its small-family-business base and flat-tax line make heavy inheritance taxes unlikely.

basic-income.rationale: It attacks southern welfare clientelism and favors work, so unconditional income is unlikely.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Small-producer protectionism sits against libertarian and export-oriented northern business interests.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The party attacks Roman state interference and wants fiscal federalism and deregulation.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Its early support came from artisans and small businesses squeezed by liberalization, favoring widely held small property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Entirely foreign to a movement of small business owners and workers.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Hostile to the euro but no documented call to abolish central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No documented corporatism; the party was anti-monopolist and libertarian in orientation.

one-party-rule.rationale: The declaration invokes free institutions and constituent assembly; a one-party state is not part of the ideology.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The declaration proclaims a federal republic, so monarchy is not part of the programme.

democracy-best.rationale: The declaration grounds secession in popular constituent power and free institutions, and the League claims to speak for the voters against Rome.

direct-votes.rationale: The party held an independence referendum and favoured referendums; northern regions later held autonomy referendums in 2017.

workers-councils.rationale: Wholly alien to the movement's small-business, federalist outlook.

right-to-secede.rationale: The declaration rests on a natural right of self-determination allowing a people to dissolve its ties and form its own state.

natural-rulers.rationale: Populist anti-elite framing; though northerners are portrayed as more productive than southerners, it does not claim a natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: The movement pursued symbolic secession and electoral politics, though rhetoric occasionally flirted with force.

war-builds-character.rationale: No documented glorification of war; the movement's themes are fiscal and cultural.

separate-church-state.rationale: The party alternated between anti-clericalism and a pro-Church stance, so there is no settled view.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: It never sought scriptural law, though it later invoked Christian identity against Islam.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Libertarian rhetoric does not extend to privatizing courts and defense, which a Padanian state would hold.

military-superiority.rationale: Not an issue the movement addressed.

ethnic-nation.rationale: It builds a Padanian people from Celtic and Lombard heritage and treats the nation as a historic-cultural community.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement frames conflict as north versus Rome and south, not class, and promotes cooperation of producers.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Meritocratic and productivist northern outlook, with grievance about transfers to the South.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: By analogy it claims that Padania's native people have a right to its territory; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: It describes the Italian state as colonial toward the north, yet this concerns Italy not overseas empire; reparations unlikely.

civilizational-union.rationale: It envisions a Europe of the Regions and Peoples, but its Islam hostility implies Christian-civilization sympathies; split.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; fiscal self-interest of the north is central but not a moral doctrine.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Communitarian identity politics coexist with libertarian rhetoric.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No documented position; early Celtic neo-pagan themes were marginal.

limit-population.rationale: It opposes immigration-driven growth but is not a population-control movement.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement celebrates northern industry and productive enterprise.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Unaddressed; anti-elite populism implies distrust of technocratic delegation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Unaddressed; libertarian and security impulses split.

restore-past-order.rationale: It invokes a mythic Celtic and medieval past but is a modern political project.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatic coalition behavior was typical, but the movement is ideologically driven on the north question.

direct-action.rationale: It worked through elections and symbolic acts, not direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Padanist sources say nothing about prefiguring the desired society in methods, so this is left neutral.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The movement celebrates productive northern industry.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The declaration complains that northern wealth funds southern welfare, the opposite of need-based distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: Pro-business orientation rejects this socialist formula.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The base is made of small business owners who see profit as earned.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Alien to a federalist, electoral, business-oriented movement.

collective-farming.rationale: Not consistent with its small-property orientation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: No such theory; the party is business-friendly.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anti-tax rhetoric was strong but the party wants a Padanian state collecting all taxes, so it is not anti-tax in principle.

harm-principle.rationale: Unaddressed; libertarian rhetoric versus conservative social line.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The declaration is built on the collective rights of peoples, while the party also defends the Popolo Padano as a group.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Secession is exit for a region, but it also stresses voting and reform.

state-as-business.rationale: It wants a smaller, cheaper state yet not customer-style governance.

positive-liberty.rationale: Libertarian-leaning economics rejects material-means conceptions of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: It cast itself as defying elite media; media was seen as hostile, though the party also ran its own outlets.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The party's focus is cultural not biological, though some members used slurs about southerners.

organic-representation.rationale: It sought a Europe of the Regions and Peoples but there is no documented corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: Hostile to the centralist state; wants smaller state and federalism.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement framed the north's reawakening against Roman decadence, but the language is regionalist.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Its territorial aims are limited to separating Padania, not expanding abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: It proposes a republic, not feudal personal loyalty.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: It claims its history and geography are natural truths while rejecting Rome's narratives; not a relativist.

universal-morality.rationale: The movement rests on particular northern identity rather than philosophical claims about universal morals, and no stance is documented.

single-common-good.rationale: No Padanist text addresses common good versus competing interests; its politics is openly one of regional interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The party has varied; some figures were pro-Israel in anti-Islam alignment, but no core position.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Unaddressed; the movement concerns domestic regionalism.

revive-national-language.rationale: The declaration says the school system suppressed local languages, implying support for reviving them, though Italian remains the state language.

school-vouchers.rationale: Libertarian and small-state leaning with grievance at centralized school system; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal frugality and complaints about Roman waste suggest agreement, though not stated.

economic-freedom.rationale: The original programme called itself federalist libertarianism.

rule-by-example.rationale: The movement relies on laws, referendums and electoral politics and takes no documented view on rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The declaration asserts a natural right of every people to self-determination and to choose its own government.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign-policy use of force is outside the movement's concerns, so no position is inferable.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement invoked both Celtic and Catholic symbols without a stance on reason versus faith.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The party's rhetoric stresses reserving benefits and housing to natives and opposes irregular immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The productive-north and anti-clientelism themes make work conditions natural; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: The party described itself as neo-labour and appealed to employers and workers together as northern producers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: It exalts cultural heritage and tradition.

workers-nation.rationale: The party organized workers on territorial and national lines, as northern producers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatism suggests lean but no explicit position.

ban-interest.rationale: A pro-business movement would not do this.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Cultural nationalism, not legal racial segregation, was the party's stance.

state-class-instrument.rationale: It sees the Roman state as the north's exploiter, not as a class instrument.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy was not part of the Padanist programme and no documented position exists.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The party sees Islam and irregular immigration as threats to identity and tradition, implying an expectation of assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: The party's most extreme voices may allege this, but it was not core Padanian doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Unaddressed; the League benefited from various systems.

national-mission.rationale: It speaks of cooperation, tolerance and peace, not missionary spread.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement is strongly anti-elite and styled itself against a corrupt Roman party system; Roma Ladrona.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past security-force abuses is not an issue the movement raised.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Libertarian rhetoric supports a small state, but Padania would assume all state powers.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Hostility focuses on culture and Islam, not interracial marriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formally yes, but northern-versus-southern stereotypes undercut it.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement uses colonial language about Rome's rule over the north but takes no documented view on settler states in general.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Unaddressed; anti-Islam rhetoric yet no conversion limits.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Irrelevant to the movement; northern livestock interests.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Split between anti-clerical and pro-Church strands.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Irrelevant to a movement against statism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The declaration grounds Padanian sovereignty in the free consent and constituent power of its peoples.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance doctrine is not addressed in Padanist sources; northern exporters' interests are the only hint.

population-transfer.rationale: Opposes irregular immigration and returns boats, but not forced removal of resident minorities; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Unaddressed; party is not pacifist but not aggressive.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Northerners are portrayed as productive in contrast to southern parasitism, but no general doctrine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A secessionist movement itself would be exposed to such bans, so it is hostile.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The declaration accuses Rome of colonial domination, but no republican theory is stated.

separated-powers.rationale: Federal structure divides power; inferred from federalism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: It prioritizes northern producers and citizens.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing sales were a British issue and no Padanist position on social housing is documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Business base for, worker base against.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not a doctrine of the party.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: It presents Islam and immigration as threats to Padanian identity and cohesion.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The declaration appeals to free institutions; not supportive.

party-controls-media.rationale: It appeals to free conscience and institutions.

party-commands-army.rationale: A federal republic with civilian institutions, as in the declaration, leaves no place for party command of the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Hostility to immigration implies long residence requirements.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not an issue; the party criticizes political privilege though.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: No documented stance on binding party members to decisions, beyond the party's strong centralised leadership under Bossi.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The party has been strongly Eurosceptic, calling the euro a crime against mankind, though early declaration spoke of Europe of Regions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: It proclaims a federal republic, not presidential command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not a Padanist issue and the movement's relation with the Church shifted over time.

clerical-rule.rationale: Nothing in Padanist sources supports rule by religious scholars; the declaration appeals to free institutions.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Unaddressed; mild inference from conservatism but also free-speech rhetoric.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits were not addressed in Padanist texts; no inference is possible.

recall-officials.rationale: Anti-elite populism and referendums suggest sympathy.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Italy's alliances were not a Padanist issue, and the movement made no documented demand about them.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry was not part of the programme; the movement favoured law-and-order policing.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Valorizes northern local communities but also industrial producers.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: It presents Islam as a threat to its identity, implying cultural hierarchy.

death-penalty.rationale: Unaddressed; Lega figures have called for it but Italy forbids it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: No documented position on curricula of this kind; the party's Catholic-leaning conservatism implies mild opposition at most.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The party never made pornography a cause and adherents are split between libertarian and conservative strands.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: It defines the Padanian people by ancestry and heritage, and opposes easy naturalization.

minority-language-support.rationale: The declaration complains that the state school system suppressed local languages and identities.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Mill-style views on social conformity are not discussed; the movement stresses communal identity but also libertarian rhetoric.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Third-world debt was not a Padanist issue, and fiscal frugality points both ways.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: It couples independence with fiscal control; Padania would collect all taxes.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1996 declaration was issued by a self-styled Constituent Assembly of northern delegates in Venice.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Opposes redistribution even domestically toward the South.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons were not discussed by the movement, whose sovereignty concerns were fiscal and territorial.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Padanist sources propose a federal republic without specifying how its head of state would be chosen.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Hostility to the euro and the ECB is documented, but libertarian sympathies favour sound money, so adherents split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial settlement for peace is outside the movement's concerns.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Padanist small-property outlook protects ownership, but no source frames it as conditional on the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union's character is not a topic the movement addressed.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance obligations were not a Padanist topic and no position is documented.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The declaration calls Italian rule colonial but doesn't treat occupation law.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The declaration specifies a republic but not the role of its head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: As a secessionist movement it denies that the state may force a region to stay.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Federalism and autonomy within a larger state were its fallback position.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Padania was proclaimed a federal republic, leaving no place for a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The party approved a flat tax at its 2014 congress.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement emphasises inherited culture and heritage, but takes no stand on nature versus nurture.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Contradicts its appeal to free institutions.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy was not part of the movement's concerns.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Constitutional theory of mixed government is absent from Padanist sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Bossi's personal leadership was heavily promoted but it wasn't doctrine.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy was not addressed by the movement.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Socialism-state theory is entirely foreign to a federalist, small-business movement.

land-redistribution.rationale: Contrary to the small-property, pro-business base.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement did not address refugee return, though its hostility to immigration limits sympathy to arrivals.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Padania is claimed for a self-defined people, but not beyond Italy's borders.

women-must-cover.rationale: It opposes Islamic practices as a threat to identity and has pushed bans on face coverings.

common-currency.rationale: The party ran on Stop the Euro and Salvini called the euro a crime against mankind.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: It claims Celtic and Cisalpine ancestry and has had Celtic ties (Pan-Celtic themes), but the main project is Padania.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: It claims local autonomy over language, schooling and culture against the centralized state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Persecuted-minority strategy is not a Padanist matter and no position is documented.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fiscal grievance is central but the movement stresses identity.

no-bailouts.rationale: Opposes Roman waste and southern subsidies, so inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The declaration criticizes the judiciary and populism favors majorities, though federal structure limits.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Export-oriented northern industry would not wish exclusion from trade.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The movement criticises globalisation but offers no documented view on binding standards in trade deals.

moral-incentives.rationale: Replacing material incentives with moral ones is foreign to a movement centred on productive northern enterprise.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The party works through elections and symbolic acts.

history-own-civilization.rationale: It complains that Italian school history suppressed local identities and builds a Padanian historical narrative.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: It denounces Italian rule over the north as colonial, and rejects domination by one people over another.

patriotic-education.rationale: It adopted a flag, anthem (Va' Pensiero) and symbols to teach Padanian identity.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposes special treatment, inferred from its right-wing outlook.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The party's pro-market, pro-business stance implies confidence in capitalism's resilience, though this is inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Labor-aristocracy theory plays no role in Padanist thought and no stance is documented.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Unaddressed; its text affirms free institutions.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Unaddressed beyond its own colonial analogy.

minority-veto.rationale: No Padanist source argues for consent-based minority vetoes; the movement itself seeks majority rule in a federal order.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The declaration says the state ignored protests and justifies throwing off its authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics was not a Padanist topic, so no position is documented.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use was not addressed beyond northern agricultural interests, so no position is documented.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement stresses fiscal fairness for producers rather than elite duties to the poor, and no stance is documented.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt-school cultural criticism is not part of Padanist thought, so no position is documented.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is foreign to the movement, which blames Rome as an exploiter and takes no stance on this.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: It argues the North is drained by Rome, a domestic analogy, but not the world system.

native-born-offices.rationale: Priority for natives is a general theme.

party-own-road.rationale: The question concerns communist parties and has no bearing on Padanism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Developing-country aid policy was not part of the programme, so no position is documented.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Priority for native Padanians in Padania.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Split; Lega is mixed, with some members hostile to it.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American Civil War historiography is not a Padanist topic.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed by Padanist sources; socially conservative lean suggests mild sympathy but nothing is documented.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed in Padanist sources, so no position is documented.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: It sees Islamic culture as incompatible with Padanian tradition.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not addressed in Padanist sources; the party's family politics is conservative but no stance on paying care work is documented.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment method is not a Padanist topic, though the movement criticises Roman patronage.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not addressed in Padanist sources and adherents differ between libertarian and Catholic leanings.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding delegates was not a Padanist proposal, though populist sympathies exist.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The party defended state pensions in 1994 and favors libertarian ideas.

single-official-language.rationale: It criticizes suppression of local languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in Padanist sources, and pro-business and anti-foreign sentiments pull opposite ways.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A right-wing, anti-affirmative-action outlook implies rejection, but this is inferred, not stated.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The movement celebrates northern enterprise and prosperity and has no documented critique of consumerism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed in Padanist sources; sovereigntist impulses favour it but libertarian ones do not.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Native-first, reluctance on immigration suggests this.

residents-only-property.rationale: Localist and native-first impulses imply sympathy for residents-only purchases, but this is inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations theory is not part of Padanist thought, so no position is documented.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Unaddressed in principle, though its declaration disclaims Rome's authority.

non-intervention.rationale: Non-intervention doctrine is not addressed in Padanist sources, although the movement demands freedom from Roman interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not addressed in Padanist sources, so no position is documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Padania claims a unity within Italy's borders; the principle of reunifying nations divided by outside powers does not apply.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Party propaganda framed Islam as a threat and some figures alleged plots, but this was not core Padanian doctrine.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The party's socially conservative drift is incompatible with ending legal marriage.

local-production.rationale: Support for local artisans and small business suggests sympathy, though export industry matters too.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is organized as a formal party with a federal structure.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Eurosceptic stance and calls for sovereignty over EU rules imply priority of national law.

religious-nation.rationale: It defines Padanians by territory and heritage, with inconsistent religious themes, not by shared religion alone.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Irrelevant to a movement asserting sovereignty.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The declaration says Padania would collect all taxes and complains northern wealth funds the South; fiscal federalism is core.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed since communal ownership of means of production is rejected anyway.

defeat-communism.rationale: Right-wing outlook suggests agreement though not a defining theme.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Pro-market and regionalist healthcare approaches favor mixed provision; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: Lega Nord defended Catholic and Christian identity against Islam, so it rejects religion as a fading illusion; inferred from its identity politics.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Its small-business, libertarian economics treats private enterprise as the engine of northern prosperity; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The movement is socially conservative and market-leaning, so it would see equality as not requiring economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Its social conservatism and defence of the family point to private family care; inferred from the party programme.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The declaration promotes local languages and dialects rather than a purified standard; no purge policy is documented, so mild disagreement is inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: The movement did not address treaties with internal nations; it wanted self-rule for itself, and adherents would not clearly take either side.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Its federalism is built on nation-like regions, markets and private property, the opposite of common-property communes; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: It sought northern self-rule and hostility to internal redistribution, not state-steered settlement; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: It rejected communism and central planning but favored markets, so it is not a third-way movement; adherents are not framed this way in the sources.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of a native northern Padanian identity against newcomers and Rome; no explicit land-claim doctrine is documented.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: the movement was a mainstream regional party whose programme and declaration never touch the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: the party opposed expanding gay rights but its programme never sought criminal penalties.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The 1996 declaration proclaims a democratic federal republic of Padania, with no place for suppressing opponents.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: Lega Nord defended Christian identity against Islam but its liberal-libertarian wing did not seek blasphemy penalties.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the movement was anti-statist and focused on self-rule within Europe, with no overseas-empire agenda.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the movement framed Islam as a threat to identity and would not endorse a Muslim duty of resistance.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to political Islam and its claim to a democratic constitutional order.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from its demands for local self-rule, devolved powers and direct referendums.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: it was a regional right-populist movement hostile to leftist identity-politics frameworks.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the party's social conservatism on family and sexuality.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from its Catholic-leaning social conservatism, though its libertarian wing may differ.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: it presented itself as defending northern interests beyond the traditional left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: its small-business and libertarian base did not use Marxist ideas of alienation.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Scholarship documents the Lega's portrayal of Islam as a threat to the Padanian people's identity and values.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: the declaration grounds sovereignty in the people, not God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the Lega opposed veils but defended the crucifix in public places, so adherents are split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The party has no documented line on harassment complaints and NDAs.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred from its libertarian economics and flat-tax advocacy, though it also defended pensions.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: it wanted self-rule and its own northern security structures, not disarmament.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from its view that the productive north should not be held back by redistribution to the South.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: the movement was Eurosceptic but never took a clear line on military blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The 1996 declaration proclaims a federal republic, so inherited supreme office does not fit the programme.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the movement's libertarian, small-business and flat-tax economics, which favor market banking over cooperative credit schemes.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the Euroscepticism and the demand that the North, not Rome or outside bodies, set its own fiscal course.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the declaration's democratic self-rule framing; no wealth qualification for voting appears in the sources.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Never addressed; the movement is regionalist and libertarian, and ecological or feminist domination theory is not part of it.

reification.rationale: Inferred from its market-friendly small-business politics; a critique of commodity relations is absent from the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from its defence of private enterprise and its own use of party media; no complaint about wealth-owned media is documented.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the attack on a clientelist Roman state that rules by favours rather than by even-handed law.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Padanian identity is cultural and territorial rather than a formal racial franchise, and the sources document no call to limit the vote by race.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the party favored direct democracy and referendums, but internet participation is anachronistic for the period.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Rome, anti-corruption stance, which favors exposing how the central state allocates money.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Hostility to Islam is cultural and about immigration; no legal restriction on interreligious marriage is documented.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The anti-Islam stance targets immigration and identity rather than organized shop boycotts, which the sources do not mention.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; the movement favored referendums and direct democracy but no sortition body is documented.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Little documented; the movement defended Christian identity against Islam but took no position on reinterpreting doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the Lega Nord's small-business, anti-tax libertarian strain, which rarely treats private wealth as a danger; its targets are Rome and the South.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Lega Nord members were split, with the party's Catholic-identitarian wing hostile to gay rights while others accepted civil liberties; no stated position.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of northern Christian identity against Islam and its hostility to atheist-communist state control.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Inferred from the party's law-and-order platform and its calls for tougher policing of crime and illegal immigration.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the movement's federalism and demand for self-rule for northern communities within or beyond Italy; consociational wording was not used.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to the Roman state and its clientelist spending, and its preference for local solutions.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from its anti-establishment attack on career politicians in Rome; no formal term-limit proposal is documented.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its party structure built around a strong leader, Bossi; no interest in liquid democracy is documented.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred from its concern with regional, fiscal and immigration issues; existential-risk policy never appears in its sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the party's Catholic-identitarian and traditionalist wing, which defended church custom; no stated position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from adherents split between traditional family-values voters and a modern northern workforce; no stated position.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the Lega's hostility to illegal immigration and Islam, described in the sources, which makes granting foreigners a vote very unlikely.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the movement's small-business, regional libertarian politics, which dislikes price caps.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the same market and small-business orientation; not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Lega fielded Green Shirts and the Padanian Guard, but the sources do not describe drilled youth training, so adherents are split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's quarrel is with Rome, not with foreign basing.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no known stance.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the anti-clientelist, pro-small-business view that attacks Roman and southern unearned dependence.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defensive, law-and-order outlook; not discussed in the sources.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Bossi's rhetoric invoked a Celtic and Lombard continuity for Padania; inferred from that, as the sources do not detail it.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the movement's traditionalist, Catholic-identity stance; not addressed in the sources.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the same traditionalist stance; not addressed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The movement had its own rites and secession-era symbolism but no clear cult of martyrs; adherents are split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred; the movement's politics is fiscal and identity-based, not framed as good against evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The 1996 declaration aims to gather the northern people in their own state, not to serve a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement pursued political self-rule and fiscal federalism first, as its programme shows.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of a Catholic northern identity; not addressed in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the same defence of traditional Catholic identity.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of northern identity against immigrants and its southern-dependency complaint.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The movement's defining claim is that the northern regions form one nation, Padania, which the 1996 declaration treats as a single unit.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Lega Nord's anti-Rome, anti-party-state populism and its claim to defend northern workers; not documented directly.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from the movement's small-business, regional-libertarian politics, which reject class-based socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Regional control of public services is standard autonomism, but its libertarian side favours privatisation; no stated line.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from Lega Nord federalism, which proposed a federal senate representing regions.

municipal-property.rationale: Its small-business, free-enterprise base rejects communal ownership of production.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Miglio-style federalism favours strong regions, but a coordinating confederation of towns is not documented.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the party's traditionalist, family-centred northern identity politics; not documented directly.

anonymous-payments.rationale: No documented position; its anti-Rome fiscal rhetoric and the state's authority pull in different directions.

person-over-state.rationale: The movement stresses the northern community against Rome and hostility to Islam, but states no general doctrine on person and state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from its defence of northern Christian identity against Islam; no doctrine on human nature is documented.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Padanists demand self-rule secured against Rome, with independence as the final goal, so revocable powers are rejected.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the party's defence of northern local agriculture and products; not documented in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from its small-town and small-business northern base and hostility to big-city Rome; no stated position.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Padanian identity is territorial and cultural, not racial; the sources frame the nation as a northern people, not a race.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in northern identity is central, but pride in race or ancestry as such is not the doctrine's framing.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the party's focus on regional self-rule, not foreign adventure; no stated defence doctrine.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Padanists defined the Padanian people by shared northern identity and promoted local languages, but their nation rested on territory and grievance against Rome more than on one language, so agreement is moderate.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the 1996 declaration's secular federal republic of individual citizens; nothing documented supports religious separate electorates, and the party was hostile to Islam.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred from Lega rhetoric blaming Rome and a centralist elite; secessionists often cast outside forces as hostile, but no specific foreign partition plot is documented.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from libertarian, small-business and low-tax politics that favored tuition and local control over tax-funded free services; not documented.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the party's anti-tax, small-business stance; no environmental tax programme is documented and new taxes cut against its fiscal message.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of inherited northern identity and territory, which implies a duty to hand things on; no environmental statement is documented.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; the party's social conservatism points one way and its mixed record on gender politics the other.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; Lega Nord was Eurosceptic and hostile to illegal immigration, and security-minded, with no stated position on arms levels.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed; Bossi's populism attacked opaque Roman elites, which suggests mild sympathy for openness, but no position on secret treaties is documented.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian, business-friendly economics and flat-tax ideas, though Euroscepticism pulls some the other way.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Lega Nord had its own uniformed Padanian Guard and a pro-gun-ownership base, so a strict state monopoly is inferred as rejected.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The 1996 declaration treats Padania as a nation with the right to self-defence, so refusing orders to fight is inferred as unwelcome.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The movement's small-business base favours firm-level pay over union-set rules.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the small-business, anti-tax stance of the Lega Nord; transfers to low earners were not a priority.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Fiscal federalism and complaints that Rome wastes northern taxes imply support for limits on state borrowing, though no specific rule is cited.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not addressed directly; the movement's focus on northern interests and hostility to foreign groups imply little sympathy for redistribution to developing countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement attacks the Roman state and proclaimed independence, but pursued it through elections and declarations, not revolution.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Self-rule and fiscal federalism let regions set their own arrangements, which is close to the statement's idea.

sacred-nation.rationale: Padania is claimed as a natural nation with its own identity, and the 1996 declaration speaks of its sovereignty; the sacred wording is stronger than the sources.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the small-business, low-tax orientation; the movement did not campaign for student debt relief.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The movement claims the opposite direction: a wealthy north exploited by Rome and the south, so the statement as worded is not its view.

shared-human-nature.rationale: No stated view; the movement's defence of northern identity and hostility to Islam point away from universalism but no doctrine is documented.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: the Lega Nord attacked the Roman-run state broadcaster as a centralist institution and favoured regional control.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of a northern Christian identity and hostility to Islam, which treats religions as distinct, not one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not a defining issue; the party defends northern producers but opposes subsidies flowing south.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; Italy has no national arsenal to keep.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the Lega's cross-class territorial politics, which puts north against Rome and rejects class-based parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the movement's hostility to Islamic immigrant practices; the sources do not discuss the issue directly.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the liberal, small-business outlook; the sources do not discuss the issue.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the movement's promotion of regional Lombard and Venetian dialects as distinct heritage rather than one Italian language.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The libertarian small-business strand might favour liability over agencies, but the sources do not say.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the secular, modernising, anti-clientelist programme, which has no place for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the libertarian small-business politics, which resists regulation of enterprise.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the party's law-and-order stance on crime and immigration.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the hostility to illegal immigration and Islam, which expects newcomers to assimilate to northern identity.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Lega Nord's libertarian, small-business politics favour voluntary arrangements over compulsion; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: The movement's focus on citizenship, illegal immigration and the Padanian people points to strict voter eligibility checks; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The movement defended northern Catholic identity against Islam and favoured privileging the native culture; inferred from its identity politics.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The 1996 declaration grounds the state in popular self-determination and a federal republic with elected bodies; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Lega Nord combined social conservatism with a largely secular northern base, so adherents are split.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Its libertarian streak and distrust of central power suggest opposition to such state powers; inferred.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The party's flat tax and anti-welfare-bureaucracy economics fit a single simplified payment; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: No Padanist text questions equal suffrage, and the declaration speaks of the rights of all citizens; inferred.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Lega rhetoric blames Islam specifically for women's status, not religion in general; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: The movement defines Padania by culture and people, not officially by biology, but its identity talk is often ethnic; adherents split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Its hostility to Roman bureaucracy and big government suggests it would not favour new dedicated agencies; inferred.

missingStatements.text: A people may declare independence from its state by its own decision, even if the state does not agree.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1996 declaration was a unilateral proclamation of independence grounded in the natural right of self-determination.

missingStatements.text: Rich regions should not be required to subsidize poorer regions of the same country.
missingStatements.rationale: The core grievance is that northern taxes fund the clientelist South, and the declaration claims all taxes for Padania.

notes: Positions are those of the Bossi-era Padanist core; Salvini's Lega since 2013 has shifted toward Italian nationalism. Early Padanism also had Celtic neo-pagan and anti-Catholic strands, so religion answers are mixed. Most economic and social answers are inferred, so confidence is low.
